findings.namedBuyers: Bulent Karabagli and Lina Chan are both explicitly named festival organizers and full-time teachers behind Argentine Tango Toronto. Both are relevant first contacts for accommodation referrals, visiting-artist lodging and determining whether anyone purchases rooms centrally. Their organizer roles do not establish hotel-contract authority. Public shared organizer email: bulentlina@gmail.com; official contact form is available.
findings.futureEdition: Official 2027 schedule, registration and venue pages publish September 22–26, 2027, Toronto. First workshop: September 22 at 8:15 pm. Sunday September 26 closing milonga runs 9 pm–1:30 am or later, crossing into September 27. Homepage banners say September 22–27 while its FAQ says September 22–26; retain September 26 as the published programme end date and confirm final departure needs rather than silently extending the edition. This is an announced edition within the requested horizon, not extrapolated recurrence. Registration terms mention credits for a 2028 festival, but no exact 2028 dates or venue were established.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown is a possible supplementary city-hotel option for visiting dancers, artists or organizer-paid guests, not the festival venue. The published venue is downtown but away from the hotel’s Harbourfront location; do not sell this as MTCC-generated demand or assume venue-adjacent convenience. A limited negotiated allocation could fit a 157-room hotel if overnight demand, budget and travel arrangements are confirmed. No evidence establishes 15–109 peak rooms, any minimum room yield, or exclusive housing feasibility. Studio programming is already located elsewhere; do not propose relocating the entire dance event into the hotel’s smaller single ballroom or assume dance-floor/catering capability. Resort positioning is irrelevant to this urban event.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: Argentine Tango Toronto by Bulent & Lina, 206 Beverley Street, Toronto, Ontario M5T 1Z3, Canada. Toronto proper, downtown near the University of Toronto/Kensington Market; not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The organizer advertises five dance studios over two floors, approximately 2,500 sq ft main hall plus 1,500 sq ft Milonga Ocho hall, and capacity 500. Capacity is not attendance. This is a published venue commitment, not proof of a signed contract or available hotel inventory; it is not a competing hotel.
findings.historicalRotation: Retrieved 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 records all identify 206 Beverley Street in Toronto, as does the 2027 announcement. Evidence supports a recurring Toronto studio-based event, not destination or host-hotel rotation. Some historical listings disagree on start/end dates; those conflicts are retained in the edition timeline. No earlier venue sequence was established.
findings.accommodationSourcing: The edition-specific 2027 page is headed “WHERE TO STAY” and “Airbnb / Hotel Search Tool Below.” It lists: Hotel Ocho; DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Toronto Downtown; Holiday Inn Toronto Downtown Centre; Beverley Place; SONDER The Beverley; SONDER The Slate; Dragon Gate Inn; University of Toronto Residence; Chestnut Residence; The Rex Hotel Jazz & Blues Bar; Elegant Suite at Bloor/Bathurst; Ration | Beverley; The Palmerston. Examples include “Right next to the venue” for Beverley Place and “walking distance to Argentine Tango Toronto by Bulent & Lina” for several properties. Interpretation: attendee self-search/recommendations, not verified contracted housing. No room-block code, allocation, housing bureau, host-hotel agreement or open RFP is published on the reviewed accommodation and registration pages. Hotel contracting status remains unconfirmed. These names are reproduced as published recommendations, not verified current operating brands, availability or commitments; the extensionless accommodation page still carries 2026 dates.
findings.organizationStructure: Organizer-operated Argentine tango school and event-production programme: Bulent & Lina / Argentine Tango Toronto. Official biography describes teaching, choreography, workshops, milongas and festival organization. This is not evidenced as an association congress or an agency/PCO/DMC-managed event. Legal entity, ownership form and any external accommodation intermediary remain unverified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The accommodation page emphasizes inexpensive options and proximity to 206 Beverley Street, including B&Bs, residences and budget rooms. Those are practical competitive advantages against a Harbourfront stay, but not evidence of contracted incumbents. The organizer advertises hundreds of dancers; the 2025 listing expected 350, not verified actual attendance or 2027 demand. No published sellout, overflow requirement, room-night figure, peak-room figure or displaced business was found. Do not convert venue capacity 500 into hotel demand.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Bulent Karabagli and Lina Chan together through bulentlina@gmail.com or the official form. Reference the September 22–26, 2027 programme and ask whether any visiting-artist rooms are organizer-paid, whether delegates self-book, whether existing hotels have agreements, and whether an additional hotel recommendation or small allocation would help. Confirm September 27 departures after the overnight closing milonga, expected non-local guests, room budget, booking/pickup history and purchaser authority before quoting. Offer lodging-first options subject to hotel availability; verify dance-floor and food-service capability internally before proposing any side event. Do not displace the published venue or claim overflow.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the target 2027 edition, event attendance registration is published and the non-hotel venue is selected. Access to accommodation purchasing is unconfirmed: approach the named organizers for introductions or a referral-rate discussion, not an assumed live RFP. No evidence shows lodging committed exclusively elsewhere; equally, absence of a published block does not mean sourcing is open. The 2026 edition is historical as of November 16, 2026.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: pursue a place on a future accommodation recommendation page and explore a small visiting-artist or attendee allocation while leaving the studio venue intact. Official annual wording and multiple historical editions support recurrence; registration terms also refer to 2028 credits. Neither proves a future open hotel requirement or an announced, dated 2028 edition. Treat later-cycle capture as relationship development until organizer need and decision timing are verified.
